newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Senate delays review of telecoms bill.
newsitem.headline: Italian Senate delays review of telecoms bill.

text.p: The Italian Senate will debate a controversial bill covering the creation of a watchdog authority for the telecoms sector and antitrust regulations for television, on May 20, and not May 13 as previously scheduled.
The bill must be passed into law before Italy can push ahead with the much-delayed privatisation of telecom holding Stet, slated for this autumn.
Undersecretary at the post and telecommunications ministry, Michele Lauria, told Reuters the debate had to be put back because of a packed Senate timetable over the next three weeks.
However he said the bill could still be approved by the May 31 deadline set by Post Minister Antonio Maccanico.
Lauria said Senate approval was the main obstacle in the path of the legislation. "Once we have Senate agreement, the time (for full ratification) will be very rapid," he said.
Under Italian law both the Senate and lower house of parliament have to approve a bill before it becomes full legislation.

After months of negotiations, the centre-left government reached a deal with the centre-right Freedom Alliance opposition over the bill on Tuesday, persuading the Alliance to drop 2,500 amendments it had attached to the draft law.

However the separatist Northern League party immediately tabled the amendments again, under its own name. The decision could cause further lengthy delays to the reading of the bill unless the government decides to call a confidence vote.
The Freedom Alliance dropped its amendments after persuading the government to make changes to complex plans covering television ownership regulations.
